before.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
before.description: Language and meaning are situated in shared practices and forms of life. Geertz draws on this account of public meaning in interpreting culture.
before.representative_figures_and_works: Philosophical Investigations (1953). This is the later Wittgenstein; it is not a claim that all interpretive anthropology derives from him.

after.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
after.description: Language and meaning are situated in shared practices and forms of life. Geertz draws on this account of public meaning in interpreting culture. The Investigations examines varied uses of language, overlapping family resemblances and the practice of following rules. Skinner later explicitly credits its attention to use in developing his historical questions.
after.representative_figures_and_works: Philosophical Investigations (1953). This is the later Wittgenstein; it is not a claim that all interpretive anthropology derives from him.
after.scope_note: The later philosophy revises earlier assumptions without forming a general historical theory. The meaning/use formulation in §43 is explicitly qualified; agreement in forms of life is not a claim that majority opinion creates truth. The preface acknowledges Ramsey’s conversations and Sraffa’s criticism. Philosophical similarity to Ryle does not establish a single transmission direction.

before.label: Gilbert Ryle
before.description: Distinguishes a bodily movement from what someone is doing in a socially meaningful situation. Geertz explicitly borrows the term thick description.
before.representative_figures_and_works: The twitch and the wink: similar movements can be different actions. Ryle is the immediate source of the term, alongside Geertz’s other influences.

after.label: Gilbert Ryle
after.description: Distinguishes a bodily movement from what someone is doing in a socially meaningful situation. Geertz explicitly borrows the term thick description. The Concept of Mind (1949) challenges category mistakes in accounts of mental life and distinguishes knowing how from prior theoretical instructions. The Thinking of Thoughts (1968) develops action descriptions and exploratory thinking; Geertz adapts a distinction from this philosophical project.
after.representative_figures_and_works: The twitch and the wink: similar movements can be different actions. Ryle is the immediate source of the term, alongside Geertz’s other influences.
after.scope_note: Rejecting a hidden parallel mechanism does not deny mental processes or reduce skilled action to automatic movements. Competence, purpose and circumstances distinguish what someone does. Ryle’s account of Cartesianism is a critical reconstruction; the atlas does not treat it as an independently established history of Descartes.

wittgenstein.people: Existing individual identity preserved and selected in anthropology, philosophical debate and Skinner's contextual-history resources. Ramsey and Sraffa are added as explicitly acknowledged interlocutors, not invented historical-school founders; Austin is a separate resource in Skinner's account.
wittgenstein.works_and_arguments: Read the 1945 preface and selected complete German Investigations sections. Explain varied use, qualified meaning/use, family resemblance and rules; preserve 1953 publication and later-philosophy scope. English paraphrase is not a certified English translation.
wittgenstein.internal_distinctions: Distinguish earlier self-criticism, language games, overlapping similarities, rule-following and agreement in judgments. These distinctions appear in the individual prose and neighboring philosophical approach, without turning a person into a group or treating public meaning as majority-made truth.
wittgenstein.incoming_connections: The preface explicitly acknowledges Ramsey and Sraffa. These resources are recorded through shared people and contextual selections; their lack of individual nodes is not a reason to invent broad economic-history or philosophy influence arrows. Ryle resemblance remains undirected.
wittgenstein.outgoing_connections: Retain and strengthen the bounded Geertz influence. Add Skinner's explicitly recalled reading as a specific influence on his contextual questions, with pre-2000 reception distinguished from the 2002 interview and from all Cambridge historians.
wittgenstein.evidence_and_interpretation: German primary selections, scoped Geertz reading and Skinner's retrospective testimony support different claims. Tanney's possible reciprocal learning is qualified scholarship. Failed English access and an unused LLM rendering are recorded; Winch reception has not yet been established by a read original passage.

ryle.people: Preserve the individual identity and select Ryle as a philosophical contributor in anthropology and explanatory debate. Freud is a bounded named resource, Geertz a documented recipient and Wittgenstein a comparison; no new disciple roster is inferred.
ryle.works_and_arguments: Read Concept of Mind chapter I and II.1–3 with partial II.4, plus the entire reproduced Thinking of Thoughts essay. Explain category mistakes, knowing-how and action descriptions; retain the distinction between a philosophical inquiry into thinking and Geertz's anthropological adaptation.
ryle.internal_distinctions: Distinguish mental processes from an alleged hidden parallel mechanism, competence from automatic movement or prior theoretical recipes, and richer descriptions from extra bodily acts. Ryle's Cartesian reconstruction remains attributed rather than treated as an independently established history of Descartes.
ryle.incoming_connections: Concept of Mind p. 14 explicitly invokes Freud against assumed transparency of consciousness, supporting a narrow contribution edge. A Wittgenstein comparison preserves possible parallel or reciprocal development without claiming a settled transmission direction.
ryle.outgoing_connections: Retain the direct Ryle-to-Geertz influence and add primary conceptual context. Philosophical-debate selections identify resources for understanding action; they do not assert an unresearched transmission to Dray, Bourdieu or all practice theory.
ryle.evidence_and_interpretation: Primary OCR and a complete reproduced lecture underpin the argument; exact impression and original lecture collation remain limited. Tanney supplies an attributed counter-reading to reductive summaries, not an uncontested verdict. Erroneous publication intervals, suspect historical asides and faulty blog framing are not imported.
